description: FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.1 on risk-based approach
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.2 on national cooperation and coordination
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.3 on the money laundering offence
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.4 on confiscation and provisional measures
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.5 on the terrorist financing offence
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.6 on targeted financial sanctions for TF
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.7 on targeted financial sanctions for proliferation financing
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.10 on Customer Due Diligence
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.11 on record keeping (5-year minimum)
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.12 on Politically Exposed Persons
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.13 on correspondent banking EDD
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.15 on new technologies and virtual assets
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.16 on wire transfer Travel Rule
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.18 on internal controls and financial groups
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.19 on higher-risk countries
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.20 on suspicious transaction reporting
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.21 on tipping-off prohibition
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.22 on DNFBP CDD obligations
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.24 on beneficial ownership of legal persons
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.25 on beneficial ownership of legal arrangements
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.26 on regulation and supervision of FIs
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.28 on regulation and supervision of DNFBPs
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.29 on Financial Intelligence Units
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.30 on powers of law enforcement
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.36 on international legal instruments
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.37 on mutual legal assistance
FATF 40 Recommendations contains R.40 on international cooperation
R.1 risk-based approach is elaborated by sector-specific FATF RBA guidance documents
R.1 RBA informs application of CDD (R.10) — risk level determines CDD intensity
R.1 RBA framework informs countermeasures for higher-risk countries (R.19)
CDD (R.10) information must be retained per R.11 record-keeping requirements
CDD (R.10) is enhanced by PEP requirements (R.12) for politically exposed persons
CDD (R.10) is enhanced for correspondent banking relationships (R.13)
PEP relationships require enhanced monitoring which may trigger STR filing under R.20
R.15 (VASPs) requires application of Travel Rule (R.16) to virtual asset transfers
R.15 virtual asset requirements are elaborated in FATF VA Guidance (2021)
Travel Rule (R.16) originator/beneficiary data supports transaction monitoring and STR filing (R.20)
Group-wide internal controls (R.18) encompass group-wide CDD standards (R.10)
R.19 countermeasures against higher-risk countries requires attention to FATF blacklist
R.19 requires considering risk from greylisted jurisdictions in CDD and EDD decisions
STR reporting obligation (R.20) is paired with tipping-off prohibition (R.21)
STRs filed under R.20 are reported to the national FIU established under R.29
R.22 applies CDD (R.10) requirements to DNFBP context
R.24 BO requirements for legal persons are elaborated in FATF BO Guidance (2023)
R.25 BO requirements for trusts are elaborated in FATF BO Guidance
BO information requirements (R.24) enable FIs to verify beneficial owners as part of CDD (R.10)
R.26 FI supervision requirements parallel R.28 DNFBP supervision requirements
FIUs (R.29) cooperate internationally through channels specified in R.40 and the Egmont Group
International legal instruments (R.36) enable effective mutual legal assistance (R.37)
MLA (R.37) is one form of international cooperation covered under R.40
FATF Mutual Evaluation process assesses country compliance with all 40 Recommendations
Mutual evaluation includes effectiveness assessment via IO.1 on risk understanding
Mutual evaluation includes effectiveness assessment via IO.3 on supervision quality
Mutual evaluation includes effectiveness assessment via IO.6 on FIU intelligence use
Persistent non-compliance found in mutual evaluation can lead to blacklisting
Significant deficiencies found in mutual evaluation typically result in greylisting with an action plan
FATF publishes and maintains the 40 Recommendations
FATF publishes and maintains the high-risk jurisdiction (blacklist) three times per year
FATF publishes and maintains the increased monitoring (greylist) three times per year
FATF published the VA/VASP Guidance documents
FATF conducts mutual evaluations of member countries
Egmont Group supports FIU cooperation required by R.29
Egmont Group implements the FIU-to-FIU cooperation principles of R.40
FSRBs conduct mutual evaluations in their regions following FATF methodology
FATF × AMLR cross-reference documents EU legal transposition of FATF standards
FATF R.15 × MiCA alignment documents VASP/CASP equivalence and Travel Rule implementation
R.13 correspondent banking requirements are elaborated in FATF de-risking guidance
IO.3 effectiveness assessment directly assesses quality of AML/CFT supervision (R.26)
IO.6 effectiveness assessment directly assesses FIU intelligence and STR use quality (R.29)
IO.1 effectiveness assessment directly assesses quality of national risk understanding (R.1)
